title: Widen writer flush batch to 512 (4MB) on accepted commit_delay=0/commit_siblings=20 base
configuration_cause: wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) still leaves wal_waiting_backends.p95=1 and sync_average_ms=0.112ms; the accepted r014 bundle proved removing the fixed commit_delay stall is the dominant win, so the remaining lever is a larger writer-side flush batch to coalesce background WAL writes further without re-introducing foreground sleep.
mechanism: r014 accepted commit_delay=0, commit_siblings=20, wal_writer_flush_after=256: removing the fixed per-commit sleep cut InsertTweet p95 by 15-33% and raised TPS 16-24%. With the stall gone, the residual wal_wait anomaly is writer-side: each wal_writer wake flushes at 2MB granularity. Doubling wal_writer_flush_after to 512 (4MB) lets the background writer accumulate more WAL before issuing write()/fsync, reducing sync frequency and wal_waiting_backends queueing while commit_delay stays 0 so no foreground latency is added. commit_siblings stays at 20 to keep the (zero) group-commit window permanently inactive.
query_effect: No plan change; commit-path only. InsertTweet commit latency should stay flat or improve slightly; GetUserTweets unaffected.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: +0.3% to +1.5% successful_transaction_tps from reduced writer-side WAL sync queueing.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 flat to -2%; overall p95 unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Larger writer flush batch coalesces background WAL writes, reducing backends observed waiting on WAL.
Fewer, larger writer flushes reduce average sync time per WAL sync.
Reduced WAL wait frees terminal capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If wal_writer_flush_after=256 already saturates writer batching, doubling to 512 yields no measurable change in wal_waiting_backends.p95 or sync_average_ms.
If the residual wal_wait is foreground commit-driven rather than writer-driven, only a nonzero commit_delay would help; then sync_average_ms stays flat and InsertTweet p95 does not improve.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Keeps the proven r014 win (commit_delay=0, commit_siblings=20) intact and adds a strictly larger writer-side flush batch (256->512) to attack the remaining wal_wait anomaly without adding foreground latency.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Double from incumbent 256 to 512 (8kB units = 4MB), inside allowed [0,1024]; larger safe amplitude of the writer-side flush batching that r014 validated, still below the 1024 high bound.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; larger batch coalesces background WAL writes into fewer syncs

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Hold at 0 (allowed [0,1000]); r014 proved the fixed per-commit sleep was the stall, so keep it disabled.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Hold at 20 (allowed [0,20]); with 5 terminals this keeps the (zero) window permanently inactive.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

nodes.label: Larger writer-side flush batch coalesces background WAL writes, reducing sync frequency and wal_wait queueing
